poolinfo: Reliability-Profile Diagnostics for Partial Pooling

Source: R/poolinfo-package.R
poolinfo-package.Rd

Summarizes how much a set of estimates with known standard errors, such as the site estimates of a multisite trial, the studies of a meta-analysis or the direct estimates of small areas, can say about the individual units under a normal hierarchical model. Computes the site reliabilities and their informativeness, mean reliability, dispersion and concentration, with posterior means and intervals from numerical integration over the between-site standard deviation, design calculations, plots made with 'ggplot2', and tables and sentences for reporting. The diagnostics follow Lee (2026). Supported by the Institute of Education Sciences through Grant R305D240078 to the University of Alabama.

Details

The diagnostics describe a set of site reliabilities. A site's reliability is the proportion of the variance of its estimate that comes from the variation of the true effects; under the normal hierarchical model it is the weight of the site's own estimate, against the mean of the effects, in the site's posterior mean.

The main functions:

  • reliability_posterior() computes the posterior of the diagnostics from estimates and standard errors, by numerical integration over the between-site standard deviation.

  • reliability_profile() computes them at a given between-site standard deviation, or at the estimate of a metafor fit.

  • reliability_draws() computes them from posterior draws of another fit, such as one of brms.

  • reliability_design(), balanced_allocation() and solve_design() plan a trial.

  • compare_profiles(), report_table() and report_text() compare and report analyses.

  • plot() and the functions plot_*() show them.

vignette("poolinfo") works through an analysis, and the other vignettes cover the profiles, the posterior summaries, a multisite trial, meta-analysis, small area estimation, planning and the computation.
